the coalescing the cross-path transition window depends on, so the same-real-id cell holds that

mutations.name: K4 the receive key degenerates to the wire id, restoring id-shaped addressing
mutations.expectRed: the race: the verdict drains exactly the snapshot's delivery
mutations.cell: the race: the later arrival is neither drained nor acked
mutations.note: The degeneration a later edit could introduce as a simplification: with every receive key equal to the wire id, an id-less item's key is the empty string, the host's drain request for it matches every pending id-less delivery at once, and the framed race drains the later arrival together with the snapshot's (and the empty-request sweep returns in any shape that treats the empty string as an address). This is the original defect class back at the seam; the cell that notices first is the race cell's exact-selection assertion, which sees both messages drained where exactly one was requested.

mutations.name: K5 selection reverts to the wire id while the keys stay minted
mutations.expectRed: the race: the verdict drains exactly the snapshot's delivery
mutations.cell: the race: the verdict drains exactly the snapshot's delivery
mutations.note: The other half of the seam: the keys exist but the drain ignores them. A request holding a minted key matches no wire id, so an id-less delivery can never be drained or acked: it is re-shown on every read and redelivered forever on the durable path, the loop the receive key exists to close. Real ids still match (their key IS their id), so only the id-less cells redden.
